## You will be able to

- Attribute AI cost per team and use case
- Implement caching
- routing
- batching and caps
- Report unit economics to leadership

## Demos

| # | Demo | Module | Min | Shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `01_unit_economics.py` | 1 | 15 | a month of usage logs turned into cost per request, per resolved task and per active user, attributed by feature and team, with the margin check |
| 2 | `02_apply_three_controls.py` | 2 | 25 | six cost controls applied one at a time to the same workload, showing the saving, the quality risk and the effort of each |
| 3 | `03_dashboard_and_budget_alerts.py` | 3 | 15 | a month-to-date spend view with forecast, budget burn alerts by team, anomaly detection on cost per request and the monthly governance ritual |

## Run of show
**One week before:** `python demos/run_all.py` on the laptop you will present from — it must print `ALL DEMOS OK`. Swap `demos/data/` for the client's own examples where you can. Print `exercises.md` per table and the handout per person.
**In the room:** each demo is one command from this folder: `python demos/NN_name.py`. No internet or API key needed. Each ends with a *Say it* line — your closing sentence.
**Live mode:** set `LLM_PROVIDER` and a key in the repo `.env`; demos that benefit then call a real model.
**In the browser:** every demo also runs from the `/demos` page (section *Course labs*) — useful for sales calls and the website.
